name: 5-la
title: LA — Logical architecture
subtitle: The black box opened into logical components: the drones, the ground station and the triage unit, with every logical function allocated to one of them. Nothing physical is chosen yet.

steps.label: SHOW ONLY THE LA LAYER
steps.text: In the Explorer, ⊞ on LA scopes every diagram to the logical-architecture package. The chip above the canvas says what is shown.

steps.label: GENERAL VIEW
steps.text: All of LA, left to right: 21 logical functions, each realising an SA function and allocated to a component, the state machines and the hazards. Nothing physical yet.

steps.label: READ ONE ELEMENT
steps.text: Select a box: Properties shows what it is. fleet is the twelve identical drones, typed by SwarmMember. It gets 14 functions, the 8 coordination ones among them.

steps.label: ADD A PART BACK
steps.text: Before recording we deleted memberB, the second representative drone. Now we add it back. A new part goes under the selection, so first select LA in the Explorer.

steps.label: PLACE A PART
steps.text: Pick Part in the palette, then click empty canvas. The new part is created in LA and selected.

steps.label: NAME IT
steps.text: Type its name in Properties. With no type yet, memberB sits apart, among the boxes nothing connects to.

steps.label: TYPE IT
steps.text: In Properties, Type: SwarmMember, then Enter. The typing is bound, as the text's memberB : SwarmMember: its typed-by line is drawn and memberB moves beside memberA.

steps.label: DOCUMENT IT
steps.text: Its documentation goes in Properties, word for word as in the model: the second representative member, the other end of the peer link.

do.type: Second representative member, the other end of the peer link.

steps.label: WIRE THE PEER LINK
steps.text: In Interconnection, memberA and memberB show the ports a SwarmMember has. Pick Interface, click memberA's meshOut, then memberB's meshIn: the interface ends on the ports.

steps.label: NAME IT AND TYPE IT
steps.text: In Properties: the name peerLink and the type Common::MeshInterface, then Enter. The Text tab now has interface peerLink : …MeshInterface connect memberA.meshOut to memberB.meshIn, as before.

steps.label: THE RESULT
steps.text: memberB is back beside memberA, typed by SwarmMember and joined to it by peerLink. Not re-entered: PA's trace to memberB, which lives in PA.

steps.label: TREE VIEW
steps.text: What LA contains, one branch at a time. +N on SwarmMember opens what each member carries: its nine ports and its two state machines.

steps.label: INTERCONNECTION VIEW
steps.text: Components with ports on their edges. The eleven lines are connections: peerLink between the two representatives; fleet sends reports to triageUnit, status and tracks to groundStation; tasking and recall come back.

steps.label: ACTION VIEW
steps.text: The 21 logical functions, each allocated to a component: a set, not a sequence. Unlike SA, LA models no flows between them; what passes between components is on the connections.

steps.label: STATE VIEW
steps.text: Five state machines: a member's sortie and its condition, the ground station's duty and its link, and the mesh across the fleet. No transition has a trigger yet.

steps.label: REQUIREMENT VIEW
steps.text: The eight hazards this layer adds, all satisfied by fleet and four also by a function. The constraint at the top right is drawn here too.

steps.label: PARAMETRIC VIEW
steps.text: Five boxes, each an asserted equation over LA's own values: the coverage, the loss when one drone is lost, the share of a sector's watch a lost hand-over costs, the coverage with half the links jammed, and the unattended watch. None of these has a value of its own: the equations define them.

steps.label: CHECK
steps.text: Check reads each equation as a definition, then judges each brief target at each layer. Misses come first, as warnings: 0.78216 against the 0.9 asked for, at LA and at PA; the jamming coverage, 0.66216 against 0.75.

outro.title: PA — Physical architecture
outro.text: The components that will be built: behaviour hosted in node parts, typed physical links, units on what flows and resource budgets as constraints. The live model: cosmindxu.github.io/mbse-workflow
